claude_proposed_widenings.name: modify_age
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The potion's core effect is to reduce (or increase) the character's physical age by a dice roll amount. No v4 effect atom covers age modification. Age is not HP, AC, a condition, an ability score, a speed, or any other currently modeled quantity. A new effect atom is required.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: your physical age is reduced by 1d6 + 6 years, to a minimum of 13 years

claude_proposed_widenings.name: cumulative_use_probability
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The adverse effect on repeat consumption uses a 10% cumulative probability per prior use. This is a stateful probabilistic modifier on activation — not a save, not a fixed resource cost, but a growing chance that requires tracking the count of prior consumptions of this item type. Neither use_count resources, save_gate phases, nor any existing activation modifier expresses this shape.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Each time you subsequently drink a Potion of Longevity, there is a 10 percent cumulative chance that you instead age by 1d6 + 6 years.
